content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Status: missing (deviation — absent Customer convenience right)**

**What I found:**
- Article IV (p0049) locks us into a **36-month Initial Period**, renewable for a further seven years **at the Licensor's option**, with no Licensee right to exit on notice.
- Every termination route in the Agreement runs against us or is fault-based: Licensor may terminate immediately on *any* Licensee breach (p0049); Licensor may terminate on Licensee wind-up (p0137); the Agreement terminates automatically on a Change of Control of Licensee absent Licensor consent (p0134); Article XIX (p0132) is insolvency-only.
- Article XXI (p0138) makes the consequences of termination one-sided (return of all technology, officer's certificate, all Licensor rights survive), and Article XXIII (p0142) bars termination damages — so there is no compensating remedy for being trapped in the term.
- Helpfully, the Licensor has **no** convenience right either, so the walk-away risk on that limb is not engaged; the gap is purely our missing exit.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a new Article IV paragraph giving the Licensee a 30-day convenience exit without penalty, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming the Licensor has no convenience/without-cause right during the Initial Period or any extension — the preferred T4C position, achieved with one inserted paragraph and no edits to the existing term mechanics.

**Fallback offered in the comment:** 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, if the Licensor resists the clean 30-day exit.
